newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka helicopters attack rebel coastal camp.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka helicopters attack rebel coastal camp.

text.p: Sri Lankan air force helicopter gunships destroyed a coastal Tamil rebel camp in the northwestern Mannar district, killing at least 10 rebels, the Defence Ministry said on Friday.
The helicopters attacked the camp at Nachchikudah in Mannar, 240 km (150 miles) north of Colombo, on Thursday.
The gunships destroyed a communication tower in the camp and also sunk two large rebel speedboats which were trying to flee the base, a Defence Ministry spokesman said.
"Between 10 and 15 LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Ealam) cadres are presumed dead," the spokesman told Reuters.
The LTTE's official Voice of Tigers radio said in a Friday morning broadcast that two air force helicopters fired rockets at rebel boats, but did not say if any rebels had been killed.
The attack came a day after the rebels, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese island, reportedly captured three navy personnel.

The sailors were patrolling in a dinghy off Kalmunai Point in the northern Jaffna peninsula. Navy officials told Reuters they believe the three men were alive when the boat was captured by rebels around noon on Wednesday.
"We have asked the ICRC (International Committee of the Red Cross) to help in finding out about them and getting them back," said a navy officer, who asked not to be identified.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is higher.
